seo.title: Security and vulnerability reporting
seo.description: Where TablePro keeps credentials, what its apps send, how they are signed and updated, what Safe Mode covers, and how to report a vulnerability.

header.title: Security
header.lead: Your queries go from the app to your own database servers, never through TablePro. Here is what the apps keep and send.

bands.title: Passwords stay in your system’s keychain
text: The Mac app keeps passwords, key passphrases, AI provider keys and your sign-in in the macOS Keychain. iPhone and iPad use the Keychain too, and Linux a Secret Service keyring such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet.
iCloud Sync is off until you turn it on, and passwords sync through iCloud Keychain only if you also turn on <ui>Passwords</ui> on the Mac or <ui>Sync Passwords</ui> on iPhone and iPad.
notes: On the Mac, password sync also carries AI provider keys, never your sign-in.
A password source such as 1Password or a shell command runs a program each time you connect.

bands.title: Your queries never pass through TablePro
text: Apart from your database servers and SSH hosts, this is everything the apps send.

table.caption: What the apps send, when, and how to turn it off
rows: Usage events, never hostnames, usernames, passwords, queries or rows
<ui>Share Usage Data</ui> in the app’s Privacy settings
A daily usage report with the same limits
This computer’s name, machine ID and versions
Once you sign in: at launch and daily
Your IP address, for Mac updates and driver plugins
Update checks and a driver’s first use
Your question, the schema and the query in play
The connections and settings you choose
Off until you turn on iCloud Sync
Connections and saved queries you publish, never passwords

notes: PostHog derives a rough location from the IP address, and links usage to your account once you sign in.
Older Mac builds send usage and license checks through our server instead.

bands.title: TablePro runs no AI service
text: The assistant talks to your provider directly. The MCP server is off until you turn it on, listens on {mcpHost} only, and never shows a client a password.

table.caption: Where each AI request goes
rows: The assistant, with a cloud provider
Result rows go only if you allow them.
The assistant, with a local model
An MCP client such as Claude Code
Each request needs a token, each connection sets what clients may do, and writes pass Safe Mode.
Each tool call waits for your click.

notes: {mcpHost} says where the server listens, not who can reach it: any program on your computer, or a page open on claude.ai or app.cursor.com, can connect.
What an MCP client reads, it sends to its own AI service.

bands.title: Every build is signed, and updates are verified
text: Mac builds are signed with a Developer ID, use the Hardened Runtime and are notarized by Apple. The app installs an update only if its EdDSA signature matches the key inside the app.
On Linux, Launchpad and COPR sign the apt and dnf packages, and TablePro signs its Flatpak repository. Each file on a GitHub release has a SHA-256 checksum, and each Linux one a build attestation.
A driver plugin installs only if it matches the plugin registry’s SHA-256 and carries a valid code signature. The iPhone and iPad app comes from the App Store.
notes: The Mac app does not use the macOS App Sandbox: it runs with your user account’s access to files and the network.
A driver plugin runs inside TablePro and can read the credentials of every connection you open.

bands.title: Each connection has its own Safe Mode level
text: On the Mac the levels are {macSafeModeLevels}: Alert asks before a write, the Safe Mode levels add Touch ID or your password, the Full levels also ask before reads, and Read-Only refuses writes. At every level, DROP, TRUNCATE and a DELETE without WHERE ask first.
Linux has {linuxSafeModeLevels}, and iPhone and iPad {iosSafeModeLevels}. An organization can enforce a minimum level on its Macs.
notes: Safe Mode catches mistakes inside TablePro; for a rule that has to hold, use the database’s own privileges.
New Mac connections start at {macSafeModeDefault}, where statements run as written, the AI assistant’s writes included.

bands.title: The code is public under the AGPLv3
text: The apps are open source, paid features included, with the scripts that sign and notarize each release, so you can check this page against the code.

bands.title: Report a vulnerability privately
text: Email <securityEmail>{securityEmail}</securityEmail> or <advisory>open a private advisory on GitHub</advisory>, in English or Vietnamese, never a public issue. We reply within {businessDays}.
Name what is affected and its version, your system, the steps or a proof of concept, and what an attacker gains.
Fixes ship in a new release, so check the latest one first. There is no bug bounty program.
